To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) P450 3a is the most important P450 isoenzyme for the metabolism of a large number (hundreds) of drugs (b) its expression is regulated by induction and inhibition and (c) its catalytic activity can be predicted in vitro.

(1) P450s 3A4 and 3A5 are the major enzymes in human small bowel responsible for the biotransformations of erythromycin and its metabolites; (2) P450 3 A4 is the major enzyme in human liver responsible for the bioreduction of erythromycins; (3) P450 1A2 is the major enzyme responsible for the biodegradation of the erythromycin lactone;

(1) the metabolic transformation of drugs by P450 enzymes is an important factor in the pharmacokinetic profile of a drug; (2) the metabolism of a drug may lead to the formation of toxic metabolites; (3) P450 isozymes may be induced and/or inhibited by a given drug, thus leading to drug-drug interactions; and (4) the metabolic transformation may be predicted in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of drugs and the role of P450 in the metabolism of endogenous compounds.
the metabolism of drugs and endogenous compounds, with the regulation of P450 enzymes by drugs and with the possible consequences on drug efficacy or toxicity.
(a) the study of metabolic pathways of erythromycin and its derivatives, (b) the identification of the P450 isoenzymes involved and (c) the study of the consequences of these metabolic pathways.

the metabolism of a drug is a complex process that can be partially predicted in vitro.
metabolism is an essential step in the pharmacological action of drugs, but that the in vitro predictability of the metabolic transformation of a drug in a given organ is difficult.
the metabolism of drugs is a complex process that is not fully understood and is difficult to predict in vivo.

P450 3As are involved in the metabolism of erythromycin and that the metabolites are responsible for the P450 inhibition.
the metabolism of erythromycin is complex and that its effects on the expression of P450s are multiple and may vary according to the experimental conditions used.

the P450 system has to be studied in depth to predict the metabolic transformation of a drug and to avoid any potential adverse effects of the metabolites.
